title: Nasi Goreng (Spicy Indonesian Fried Rice)
summary: Day-old jasmine rice wok-fried with chicken thigh, shallots, chilies, galangal and shrimp paste, seasoned with kecap manis, soy and MSG, and topped with a crispy fried egg, tomato, cucumber and lime.
notes: Video: 'The Best Spicy Fried Rice Ever' on the Joshua Weissman Recipes channel (UCUAg71CJEvFdOnujmep1Svw). Written recipe for the same dish: https://www.joshuaweissman.com/recipes/best-spicy-fried-rice-recipe-nasi-goreng (prep 20 min plus day-old rice, cook 15 min; it gives no serving count). Servings (4) are our estimate: four fried eggs, one per plate. The video states the chicken, oil, shallots, green onions, chilies, galangal, shrimp paste, MSG, kecap manis, soy and garlic. From the written recipe: 4 cups (800 g) of cooked, chilled jasmine rice (the video: three and a half, maybe four cups) and 4 eggs. Our estimates: 1/2 tsp kosher salt on the chicken, galangal about 8 g for a 1-inch piece. Cucumber is half, as in the video (the written recipe says 1). Not counted: the oil for frying the eggs (3-4 Tbsp, partly absorbed), store-bought fried shallots, lime, and the optional sambal. Galangal uses USDA ginger (he says ginger works as a substitute). Shallots (2, about 80 g) and bird's eye chilies (2, about 6 g) are weighed by us; USDA's chili pepper (45 g) is far bigger than a bird's eye. Kecap manis uses a branded ABC sweet soy sauce record, shrimp paste a branded dried shrimp paste (belacan) record, MSG a branded MSG record. The crispy fried eggs count absorbed oil at our house rate (10% of the eggs' raw weight); the Fresno garnish is weighed as a jalapeño-sized chili (14 g).

steps.text: Peel and grate the galangal. Finely dice the shallots. Slice the green onion whites and greens separately. Slice the bird's eye chilies very thin and finely chop the garlic.
For serving, slice the Fresno chili, cut the tomatoes into eighths and the cucumber into thin obliques.
Heat a lightly oiled wok over high heat, add 2 1/2 Tbsp oil, then the chicken in one layer; salt it. Sear undisturbed 3-4 minutes, then stir-fry until cooked through (165°F). Remove.
Add 2 Tbsp more oil, then the shallots, green onion whites, chilies and galangal; stir-fry until softened. Add the shrimp paste and fry a few seconds until fragrant.
Add the cold rice and stir-fry 2-3 minutes, breaking it up, until hot and starting to crisp. Return the chicken, then add the MSG, kecap manis and soy sauce and toss quickly to coat.
Turn off the heat and toss in the raw chopped garlic.
Fry each egg in a generous layer of very hot oil, basting the white, about a minute, until the edges are brown and the yolk is runny.
Plate the rice with fried shallots, green onion greens, Fresno chili, cucumber, tomato, a lime cheek and the fried egg; sambal on the side.
